scope_justification: Every language is a maintained convention of signs, transmitted and reshaped by its speakers. The capacity to speak is natural; any particular language is made.
Quantity is natural, but number — the discrete, nameable, manipulable unit — is a human framework laid over it.
A made technique for fixing language in durable marks; no writing system occurs naturally.
The self is the human-idea worn by the human-animal. The animal is natural; the personal identity it maintains and presents is made.
Descent is biological, but the family — roles, names, obligations — is an enacted, made framework.
A made structural form; no arch assembles itself.
Ore is natural; the winning and working of metal is a made, transmitted practice.
A made form: nothing in nature rolls on an axle.
A coordinated craft practice — made, taught, and enacted rather than found.
Law is written coordination: fully made and fully explicit.
Money is a made agreement about value; the token is incidental, the framework is the construct.
A made lattice of personal duty — sworn, enacted, and enforced.
A made association regulating a craft; chartered and enacted.
A made fortification: matter arranged as a political claim.
A made structure whose purpose is to hold a made meaning at architectural scale.
A made instrument: metallurgy pointed at walls.
Time passes naturally, but the hour is constructed.
A made mechanism for the mass re-making of writing.
A made vessel: writing bound into a persistent, portable whole.
A made machine for executing made procedures.
A made connection of machines and, through them, of selves.
A made argument: the book in which the made world is told what it is.
A made world: every object, rule, and physical law inside it is human-written software.
A made currency within a made world.
A made bridge commodity between a made economy and the outer one.
A made organization type whose constitution is enforced by code rather than custom.
A made federation of made organizations.
A made toll structure at a made planet.
A made corporation actually operating: it holds structures, collects taxes, and pays dividends on an explicit schedule.
A made holding corporation: the thing thinged, holding the things.
A made federation bearing its claim in its name and ticker.
A made conduit whose entire function is explicit intermediation.
A human action is a corporation: this monthly performed sequence is made, patterned, and repeated.
A container is a human-made isolation framework: a set of namespace and cgroup constraints that define a bounded computational environment. Nothing in nature runs in a PID namespace.
A made framework: an operating system is authored software that governs a computer's resources; nothing in nature schedules processes.
A made agreement: a protocol is an explicit convention for exchange between machines or humans; it is authored, versioned, and adopted.
Made writing whose intended reader is a machine: authored text in a formal language, compiled or interpreted into behavior.
A made framework for remembering revisions: authored systems (git and kin) that give writing a navigable past.
A made framework for structured remembering: authored systems that hold records in queryable, durable form.
A made in-world object: EVE blueprint items are authored constructs that encode manufacture as ownable, tradeable things.
A made legal instrument: authored terms binding what may be done with a body of source code.
A made in-world object: a standing, visible offer to buy or sell at a stated price, held open by the game's market machinery.
A made framework: the promise given explicit, enforceable form between named parties.
A made technique: authored mathematics that renders writing unreadable except under stated parameters (keys).

Tool is human-made, not natural. No object in nature is a tool except by human attribution: a river is a river, a stone is a stone — they become tools only when shaped or selected by human intention to extend some bodily capacity. The distinction between tool and non-tool is a structural boundary drawn by the constructed/natural divide.

Tool is structured to persist. It is not tied to any single instantiation — a specific hammer breaks, but the tool persists through re-making across generations. Every particular tool is an instance of the form, and the form survives through the practices that reproduce it: design, manufacture, use, and the transmission of know-how. The category is self-referential: tools are what make tools.

The construct has no natural limit. Stone, wood, metal, plastic, silicon — all are substrate; the formal boundary is the relation of extension, not the material. Wherever human agency reaches beyond the body by means of an instrument, the tool appears. It is therefore as pervasive as human construction itself.

Agriculture is human-made, not natural. Wild plants become crops only through deliberate human selection, tilling, planting cycles, and culling — a set of practices that impose a constructed order on biological growth. The boundary between cultivated field and wild meadow is a structural distinction drawn by human intention, not by any intrinsic property of the land.

Agriculture is structured to persist. Farming techniques, seed stocks, seasonal calendars, and irrigation systems all reproduce across generations independently of any single practitioner. A specific field may fall fallow and revert to scrub, but the form of agriculture persists through re-manufacture: the re-sowing of known seeds, the re-cutting of furrows, the re-teaching of planting rhythms. The practice is self-referential — agriculture produces agriculture by yielding seed for the next planting.

The construct has no natural limit. Any plant or animal species can be brought under cultivation; any climate can be adapted to through irrigation, terracing, greenhouse, or hardiness selection. Wherever human agency meets biological reproduction and imposes a cycle of sowing and harvesting, agriculture appears. It is therefore as pervasive as settled human life itself.

The boundary between natural process and human-made procedure is foundational to the taxonomy. A river follows a gradient without knowing it; an algorithm is a procedure that has been formally captured so that it can be executed by any suitable substrate — stone, paper, silicon, or mind. The construct is the abstract framework of stepwise computation itself, not any particular instance of it (a specific sorting routine) nor the word for it. This entry occupies the earliest stratum of the computational branch: Babylonian arithmetic procedures, Egyptian fraction algorithms, and Euclids method of extracting square roots all predate formal mathematics as a discipline. Algorithms are the foundational construct without which computer, protocol, source-code, and database would not exist.

A human-made structured venue or mechanism where buyers and sellers meet to exchange goods, services, or claims. Distinct from market-order (a single transaction) — the market is the overarching framework that makes transactions possible. The stock exchange, the bazaar, the auction house — all are markets. Each market has rules, participants, and a matching mechanism. The construct is the venue/mechanism itself, not any particular exchange.

A legal grant of exclusive rights to an invention, issued by sovereign authority for a fixed term in exchange for public disclosure. Distinct from copyright (which covers expression — books, music, art) — patent covers functional invention — machines, processes, compositions of matter. Distinct from the invention itself — the patent is the legal construct, not the machine or process. Distinct from software-license (which governs use of software) — patent governs exclusion from making/using/selling an invention.

The taxonomy has money (mind substrate) as the abstract concept of a medium of exchange. Currency is the specific instantiation: a standardized system of money issued by an authority, with defined denominations, legal tender status, and geographic/domain scope. It fills the gap between the abstract and the particular — money is the category; currency is a member.

The taxonomy has protocol (mind substrate) — a technical agreement on data format and communication. Standard is the broader category: any convention achieving coordination across technical, social, economic, or cultural domains. A protocol IS A standard, but standards exist beyond protocols (e.g., measurement standards, etiquette, color naming). Protocol is a subtype of standard.

The taxonomy has specific behavioral patterns (feudal-obligation, poco-payout-ritual, customs) but no general tradition — the mechanism of intergenerational transmission of behavioral patterns. Tradition is what makes feudal-obligation persist across generations; it is the persistence mechanism made explicit as a construct. Distinct from custom (a single pattern) — tradition is the transmission chain itself.

A voluntary agreement between parties establishing mutual obligations. More fundamental than money (which requires contract), law (which enforces contract), and property (which is a contractual relationship). Distinct from promise (which lacks enforcement) and from law (which is the enforcement framework, not the agreement itself).

The act of comparing a quantity to a standard unit, making magnitude explicit and comparable. Distinct from number (the abstract framework of units) — number is the system; measurement is the concrete act. Distinct from counting (which enumerates discrete items) — measurement handles continuous quantities. Predates writing, predates formal mathematics.
A formal document establishing the rights, structure, and purpose of a corporation or framework. Essential to the persistence of corporate governance and legal personhood.

The charter is a human-made construct essential to the persistence of corporate governance and legal personhood. It establishes the rights, structure, and purpose of a corporation or framework; without it, a corporation has no legal standing. It sits on the human-made side of the natural/constructed distinction.

The tax is a human-made construct essential to the persistence of state revenue and sovereign authority. It is the compulsory contribution levied by law on individuals and entities; without taxation, the state has no independent means of support. It sits on the human-made side of the natural/constructed distinction.

The citizen is a human-made construct essential to the persistence of political community and the social contract. A citizen is a member of a polity with recognized rights and obligations; without this status, individuals exist outside the protective and regulatory framework of the state. It sits on the human-made side of the natural/constructed distinction.

A stargate is a human-made (or made-by-humans' predecessors) physical structure — a ring of durium alloy — that connects two distant systems in EVE Online's New Eden, enabling instantaneous travel. It is constructed, requires energy to activate, and persists through repair and refueling by player operators.

A stargate is a human-made (or made-by-humans' predecessors) physical structure — a ring of durium alloy — that connects two distant systems in EVE Online's New Eden, enabling instantaneous travel. It is constructed, requires energy to activate, and persists through repair and refueling by player operators.

A citadel is a player-constructed modular structure in EVE Online nullsec space, serving as a mobile or stationary base for corporations. It is assembled from individually manufactured modules, persists through fuel cycles and structural integrity, and is explicitly governed by the game's structure rules — no gap between its stated purpose and its function.

A planet in EVE Online is a natural celestial body made available as an economic construct through the game's planetary interaction system. While the planet itself is natural (not constructed), it becomes a corporation when humans claim it, establish extraction infrastructure, and maintain ongoing production — the parameters are claim ownership, extraction type, and resource depletion rate.

In EVE Online even nature is made: a planet is not a natural body but an authored simulation — a sphere of rock, ice, or gas placed in the universe map by the game engine, with defined resources, orbital parameters, and visual rendering. It sits on the made side because it exists only through authorship: without the universe map, the planet does not exist. Its persistence mechanism is the continued operation of the server that renders it.

A station in EVE Online is a player-constructed fixed physical structure — a hub of docking bays, industrial facilities, and offices anchored to a point in space. It is constructed from modules, requires power and fuel to operate, and persists through the server that renders it and the corporation that maintains it. Distinct from the citadel (which is mobile and modular), a station is a permanent fixture at a system's primary or secondary star.

A moon in EVE Online is an authored celestial body smaller than a planet, orbiting a planet or the system's sun. It is placed in the universe map by the game engine with defined resources, visual rendering, and gravitational influence. It sits on the made side because it exists only through authorship — without the server rendering it, the moon does not exist. Its persistence mechanism is the continued operation of the server and the mining infrastructure that corporations maintain upon it. Distinct from the planet: moons are smaller, closer to their parent planet, and typically richer in high-value ores suitable for advanced manufacturing.

A ship in EVE Online is an authored vehicle — a sphere of modules assembled into a navigable construct, rendered by the server with defined hitpoints, capacity, and speed. It sits on the made side because it exists only through the game engine: without the server rendering it, the ship does not exist. Its persistence mechanism is the continued operation of the server and the corporation that maintains and fuels it.

A smart-contract is a self-executing agreement encoded as computer software, deployed on a blockchain or distributed ledger where its persistence mechanism is the consensus of the network. It sits on the made side because it exists only through authorship — the code that defines its terms, the ledger that records its state, and the network that enforces execution. Without the software and the network, the smart-contract does not exist.

A wormhole in EVE Online is an authored tunnel connecting two distant points in the universe map — a jump-gate or natural anomaly rendered by the server. It sits on the made side because it exists only through the game engine: without the server rendering its entrance, exit, and properties, the wormhole does not exist. Its persistence mechanism is the continued operation of the server and the station or citadel anchored at its entrance.

Cloud-computing is the delivery of computing resources — servers, storage, databases, networking, software — over the internet from centralized data centers. It sits on the made side because it exists only through authorship: the virtualization software, the data center infrastructure, the billing system, and the network that connects users to resources. Without the software and infrastructure, the cloud does not exist.

Frigate is a small, fast ship class in EVE Online, designed for speed and agility over durability. Its parameters are module slots (limited), high slot count (for lasers/railguns), low slot count (for shield boosters/hull repairers), and capacitor (drives ECM, afterburners, micro warp drives). It persists through fuel (afterburner fuel or capacitor recharger O2), pilot skill (ship skills), and the server that renders it. It sits on the human-MADE side because it exists only through authorship: the ship type definition, the module blueprints, the server rendering it. Without the game engine, the frigate does not exist.

Nullsec is the unclaimed space sector in EVE Online — the collection of solar systems with security rating 0.0, where player corporations can claim territory without being part of a recognized nullsec alliance. Its parameters are system count (variable per server generation), resource yield (mining, ice, gas belts), proximity to wormholes (strategic choke-points), and distance from highsec (travel time via wormholes or stargates). It persists through the server that renders it and the corporations that claim and defend it. It sits on the human-MADE side because it exists only through authorship: the universe map generation, the security system, the wormhole network connecting it to claimed space. Without the game engine, nullsec does not exist.

A battle is a finite combat event in EVE Online between fleets of ships over contested territory, resources, or strategic position. Its parameters are start time, participants, and contested object; its persistence mechanism is recorded in-game data (killmails, event logs) and community memory. It sits on the made side because it exists only through the game engine: without the server rendering its start time, participant roster, and outcome, the battle does not exist.

Compiler is a human-made computing construct. It exists only within the authored world of software development and computing. No natural process produces a compiler. It is a fundamental construct that sits between the programmer intent (source-code) and the machine execution (computer).

Weapon is a human-made construct: instruments deliberately designed, manufactured, and deployed by humans to inflict damage or achieve tactical advantage. It sits squarely on the made side of the line, as it is an artifact of human warfare practices.

Trade is a human-made construct: the institution of voluntary exchange governed by social norms, practices, and conventions that humans have developed. It is a structured social practice, not a natural phenomenon.

Manufacturing is a human-made construct: the systematic process of converting raw materials into finished goods through organized, repeatable procedures. It is a structured industrial practice created and maintained by human institutions.

Science is a human-made construct: the systematic method of inquiry into the natural world through observation, experimentation, and reasoning. It is an organized practice created and sustained by human institutions, distinct from the natural phenomena it studies.

War is a human-made construct: organized, large-scale violent conflict between groups such as nations or factions. It is an institution created by human political organization and social structures, distinct from the natural animal aggression it channels.

Diplomacy is a human-made institution: the organized practice of managing relations between political entities through negotiation, dialogue, and compromise. It is a structured social practice created by human political organization — distinct from natural animal communication or aggression. Diplomacy persists through the institutions of statecraft (embassies, treaties, envoys) and the transmission of diplomatic knowledge across generations.

Religion is a human-made institution: organized systems of belief, ritual, and morality that structure human understanding of meaning, purpose, and the transcendent. It is a structured social practice created by human cultural and political organization — distinct from natural human psychology. Religion persists through institutions (churches, temples), texts (sacred writings), and the transmission of doctrine across generations.

Architecture is a human-made discipline: the art and science of designing and constructing buildings and other physical structures. It is a structured practice created by human technical and aesthetic organization — distinct from natural formations or the unaided human act of shelter-building. Architecture persists through the built environment itself — structures that endure for generations — and through the transmission of design knowledge across practitioners.

Property is a human-made social construct — no natural entity possesses ownership rights. Exclusive control over resources, objects, or interests is created through collective recognition, codified in law or custom, and enforced by institutions. Property persists through the ongoing social agreement that certain beings may claim exclusive use and transfer of things, and through the formal mechanisms (courts, registries, norms) that uphold those claims across generations.

A city is a human-made construct: no natural formation produces the dense aggregation of structures, institutions, laws, and social organization that defines urban life. Cities persist through the ongoing construction and maintenance of physical infrastructure, the codification of governance, and the reproduction of social agreements that coordinate millions of human lives in concentrated space.

A calendar is a human-made system for dividing and labeling the continuous flow of time into discrete, repeating units — a construct of the human mind imposed on natural cycles. Calendars persist through collective agreement to use them, institutional maintenance of the system, and cultural transmission across generations.

A bridge is a human-made structure — no natural formation is designed to span a gap with the purpose of connecting two sides. Bridges persist through their physical construction (materials, engineering) and their continued use (maintenance, replacement of worn parts).

An archive is a human-made institution — no natural process organizes records for systematic preservation. Archives persist through physical storage (buildings, containers, digital media), through cataloguing systems, and through the institutional commitment to preserve records across generations.

Bureaucracy is a human-made administrative system — no natural organization operates through hierarchical authority, written rules, and specialized roles. Bureaucracies persist through the reproduction of organizational structures, the codification of procedures, and the institutional commitment to rule-based governance.

A bank is a human-made financial institution — no natural entity holds deposits, extends credit, or intermediates between savers and borrowers. Banks persist through regulatory frameworks, capital reserves, and the trust of depositors who rely on the institution for safekeeping and lending.

Tax is a human-made compulsory contribution to state revenue — no natural process collects resources from a population for public purposes. Taxes persist through the legal authority to levy them, the administrative apparatus to collect them, and the social contract that legitimizes their use.

Government is a human-made system of governance — the exercise of authority over a territory or population through institutions, laws, and enforcement mechanisms. No natural entity governs; government persists through the reproduction of institutional structures, the legitimacy of its authority, and the capacity to enforce its decisions.

Politics is a human-made process of making collective decisions — the negotiation, competition, and deliberation through which groups allocate resources, resolve conflicts, and establish rules. No natural system deliberates about resource allocation; politics persists through the cultural practice of collective decision-making.

Audit is a human-made process of systematic examination — no natural process evaluates compliance, accuracy, or conformity against standards. Audits persist through the institutional practice of independent review, the standards against which examination is conducted, and the authority to compel access to information.

Education is a human-made process of systematic knowledge transmission — no natural system deliberately teaches another generation. Education persists through institutional structures (schools, curricula), cultural practices (teaching methods), and the deliberate effort to transfer knowledge, skills, and values across generations.

A hospital is a human-made institution for medical treatment — no natural entity provides organized healthcare. Hospitals persist through their physical infrastructure (buildings, equipment), their medical staff (doctors, nurses), and the specialized knowledge (medicine, nursing) that enables treatment.

A library is a human-made institution for the curated collection and public access of books and knowledge resources — no natural process curates published works for public study. Libraries persist through physical infrastructure (buildings, shelves), cataloguing systems, and institutional commitment to free public access.

A museum is a human-made institution for the display and preservation of objects of cultural, scientific, or historical significance — no natural process exhibits artifacts for public education. Museums persist through physical infrastructure (buildings, display cases), curation practices, and institutional funding.

A prison is a human-made institution of confinement and punishment — no natural entity incarcerates humans for violating social rules. Prisons persist through their physical infrastructure (walls, cells, security systems), their legal authority (sentencing laws), and the institutional commitment to incapacitate and rehabilitate.

A road is a human-made path for travel and transport — no natural formation is designed as a passage between places. Roads persist through their physical construction (surface, drainage, grading) and their continued use (maintenance, repair, replacement).

A map is a human-made representation of space — no natural object depicts geographic relationships in reduced form. Maps persist through their physical medium (parchment, paper, digital screen), their projection system (how 3D space is represented in 2D), and the cultural practice of cartography.

Navigation is a human-made process of planning and controlling movement through space — no natural entity deliberately plots courses between points. Navigation persists through instruments (compass, GPS), knowledge (cartography, celestial observation), and the cultural practice of wayfinding.

Communication is a human-made process of transmitting information between parties — while animals signal to each other, systematic, intentional communication with encoding, protocols, and media is a human construct. Communication persists through the medium (language, writing, signal), the protocol (rules of exchange), and the cultural practice of sharing information.

Transportation is a human-made system for moving people and goods between locations — while animals migrate, systematic organized transport using vehicles, infrastructure, and schedules is a human construct. Transportation persists through vehicles (ships, trains, planes), infrastructure (roads, rails, airports), and the institutional organization of routes and schedules.
Marriage is a human-made institution that structures partnership into a persistent social node with defined rights, obligations, and recognition mechanisms.
Labor is a human-made structuring of effort into purposeful activity, converting intention into material or intellectual outcomes through organized exertion.
Inheritance is a human-made mechanism for transferring property, status, and knowledge across generational boundaries, preserving continuity within lineages.
Craft is a human-made practice of skilled making through repeated technique, transforming raw material into objects while simultaneously developing the maker proficiency.
Festival is a human-made communal gathering marked by ritualized deviation from ordinary activity, reinforcing collective identity through shared excess and symbolic action.
Grief is a human-made social mechanism for processing loss, converting private absence into shared ritual and sustained remembrance.

Story is a human-made narrative structure that encodes knowledge, identity, and values into transmissible form, converting experience into shared meaning.
Play is a human-made structured non-utilitarian activity that develops skills, reinforces social bonds, and explores possibilities through rule-bound freedom.
Sanctuary is a human-made protected space where ordinary rules are suspended or altered, providing refuge from the ordinary social order.

Measure is a human-made standardized unit of quantification, converting continuous reality into discrete comparison through agreed reference standard.

It is constructed through trial, teaching, and cultural transmission, and persists as a technique that humans deploy to navigate complexity with bounded rationality.

the systematic study and philosophical theory of law — a human-constructed discipline that interprets, critiques, and develops legal principles through reasoned argument, academic inquiry, and the training of legal thinkers

The human-made practice of grouping entities by shared features, establishing boundaries between sets. It is a cognitive and social tool for organizing experience — not the features themselves, but the human act of partitioning the world into named groups.

Trademark is the human-made construct of exclusive rights to a distinctive sign, name, or symbol identifying commercial origin — the map that links identity to source in consumer consciousness. Made through registration, use, and legal enforcement. Persisted by renewal cycles, marketplace presence, and anti-dilution law. Not natural — animals mark territory but have no concept of commercial source-identification.

A human-made visual symbol designed to represent an organization, group, cause, or institution. It is a semiotic artifact — deliberately crafted marks, shapes, or colors assigned meaning through collective agreement, not a natural phenomenon.

The concept of affordance — a human-made construct from ecological psychology (J.J. Gibson, 1979) that names the perceived and actual properties of an environment enabling action by an agent. Not the physical properties themselves, but the MAP of action-possibilities as recognized and categorized by perceiving agents. Humans invented this concept to model the relation between environment and agent without reducing to either pure objectivity or pure subjectivity.

rubric is a human-made scoring framework — a structured set of criteria and performance descriptors used to evaluate, grade, or assess work. It is a tool for standardizing judgment, not a natural phenomenon. Created by educators, assessors, and institutions to make quality evaluation transparent and consistent.

A human-made navigational apparatus that maps terms, concepts, or subjects to their locations within a text or collection. It is the map of content organization, not the content itself — the word-structure humans built to enable reverse lookup, not the natural world.

The human-made practice of tracking the origin, history, and lineage of objects, information, and artifacts — a system of attribution that persists through documentation, citation, and chain-of-custody conventions.

A credential is a human-made marker of authorization — a token, certificate, or record that grants permission, confirms identity, or signals competence within a constructed system of trust. It is not the natural quality or skill itself, but the human institution that declares those qualities exist and are recognized.

Abstraction is the human-made practice of extracting general patterns, principles, or structures from specific instances while selectively omitting details. It is not a natural faculty — it is a constructed cognitive and methodological technique, deployed across mathematics, programming, science, and art. The map of abstraction varies across disciplines (mathematical abstraction, computational abstraction, social abstraction) but is always a deliberate human technique, never an automatic process.

Classification is the human-made practice of systematically assigning items, concepts, or phenomena into categories according to shared criteria — a cognitive and social technology for organizing knowledge so it can be stored, retrieved, and communicated across individuals and generations.

A human-made document or authorization that bridges abstract authority to concrete permission — a license, a mandate, or a justification for action, produced by institutions and recognized within legal and bureaucratic systems.

sensemaking is the human-made practice of constructing meaning from experience, information, and events. It is not raw cognition or natural perception — it is the deliberate, culturally-mediated activity of building interpretive frameworks to make the world intelligible. It persists through language, teaching disciplines, social practices, and institutional routines.

A glossary is a human-made reference structure that collects, defines, and organizes terms within a domain of knowledge. It is the map of terminology — the curated vocabulary that enables precise communication within a field, craft, or body of work.

A human-made practice of adhering to externally imposed rules, standards, or regulations. Compliance is the institutional mechanism by which organizations and individuals align their behavior with legal, regulatory, and normative frameworks. It is not a natural tendency — humans do not automatically conform to rules; they must be structured, monitored, and incentivized to do so.

A mandate is a human-made authorization that converts the will of a principal into the obligation of an agent. It is the institutionalized form of command — created by law, custom, or election, and maintained through the ongoing legitimacy of the source.

A codification is the human-made process of collecting scattered rules, customs, or knowledge into a unified, systematic form. It is an institutional act of organization — the output of human effort to make a body of information coherent, ordered, and accessible. The natural side has no codifications; they exist only as the product of deliberate structuring.

A human-made institution of formal attestation: the process by which an authorized body declares that a person, product, process, or system meets specified standards, and issues a certificate as persistent proof of that declaration. Built to persist through the certificate as a durable claim and the institutional framework that enforces it.
A formal proclamation or command issued by a sovereign authority or government, converting the will of the ruler into binding public rule

A mental model is a human-made cognitive construct — a simplified representation of reality that people create, refine, and deploy for reasoning, prediction, and decision-making. It is not the territory itself but a map built by the mind for navigating it: models are taught, shared through language and education, revised through practice, and persist across generations as cognitive tools. The natural side is the raw complexity of the world; the mental model is the human-made filter through which that complexity becomes tractable.

Framing is the human-made practice of constructing interpretive boundaries through which information, events, and ideas are selected, emphasized, and organized for understanding. It is a cognitive and social technology — not a natural feature of the world but a method humans invented to shape perception, guide interpretation, and activate specific readings. Every frame excludes as much as it includes. It persists through language, media, education, legal doctrine, and institutional communication.

Hermeneutics is a human-made theory of interpretation — the systematic framework for how texts, symbols, and actions acquire meaning. It maps the hermeneutic circle (pre-understanding to interpretation to application), not the natural act of understanding itself. Built to persist through philosophical tradition, cross-disciplinary teaching, and the institutional practice of interpretation.

A written statement of facts made under oath or affirmation, submitted as evidence or for official record. Purely human-made: it exists only through the institution of law, the practice of sworn testimony, and the legal systems that give it force. Natural speech is not an affidavit — only speech structured by law, administered by authority, and recorded in the procedures of state or court.

Official permission or approval to publish, produce, or act — a seal of institutional authorization. Purely human-made: it exists only through the authority structures (church, state, academic, corporate) that grant or withhold it. The concept itself is a map of institutional permission, not any natural phenomenon. Persists through the practices of censorship, peer review, licensing, and official sanction.
A human-made naming system that assigns standardized terms to concepts within a domain, enabling precise communication and preventing equivocation among practitioners.

Verification is the human-made practice of confirming that a claim, record, or state matches reality or an established standard. It is a map-making tool: the distinction between verification and mere assertion is a human invention, not a natural property. Verification persists through methods (inspection, testing, cross-referencing), institutions (auditors, certifiers, peer review), and protocols that standardize how claims are checked.

The formal process of confirming and giving official sanction to an agreement, treaty, or action. Humans invented ratification to create a distinct step between signing and becoming legally bound — it persists through constitutional procedure, diplomatic protocol, and organizational governance, where collective decisions require formal validation before they take effect.

Accountability is a human-made institutional construct — a system of answerability that binds agents to justify their actions to an authority or standard, built to persist through reporting structures, sanctions, and the architecture of oversight.

A formal instrument or process by which a person or body grants permission, power, or legitimacy to another to act. Human-made because it exists only through institutional frameworks — law, contract, office, or convention — and serves as a map for delegating authority in a way that no natural faculty does.

The human practice of constructing and communicating narratives — a cultural technology for transmitting knowledge, values, and identity across individuals and generations. Distinct from 'narrative' (the content/structure); storytelling is the act, craft, and social institution of making narratives.

Archetype is a human-made conceptual tool from analytical psychology — the idea that universal patterns of thought, image, and behavior recur across cultures and individuals as structured categories of the human imagination. It is not a claim about inherited biological programs but a map of the categories humans use to organize meaning, myth, and symbolic experience.

A human-made institution of systematic monitoring to ensure compliance, correctness, and accountability — established through formal roles, reporting lines, review cycles, and sanctioning authority to check the work of others

A decree is a human-made pronouncement by a recognized authority — a sovereign, monarch, executive, or tribunal — that carries the force of law or official policy within a defined jurisdiction. It is the map of top-down authoritative command, distinct from the natural impulse to direct others.

An ordinance is a human-made local law or regulation enacted by a municipal or local authority with jurisdictional force within its territorial boundaries. It is the map of decentralized legislative authority, distinct from natural community norms.

A human-made system of symbols and marks for externalizing and preserving meaning beyond immediate perception. Built to persist: notation systems (writing, musical, mathematical, notational) are engineered for transmission across time and distance, making private thought publicly accessible and durable.

A paradigm is a human-made framework of concepts, assumptions, and practices shared by a community that shapes how its members perceive, interpret, and act within a domain. It is the map of reality that a group collectively adopts — not reality itself. Scope justification: paradigms are entirely human-made social and cognitive constructs, existing only through collective adoption and maintenance. Law 2a applies: the paradigm is the map, not the territory it describes.

A human-made technique or device for augmenting recall — the map of memory-augmentation, not the natural faculty itself. Built to persist through language, teaching, and cultural transmission across generations.

The human-made process by which an authoritative body formally recognizes that an institution, program, or individual meets established standards. Accreditation constructs a public signal of trust — it is the institutionalized act of declaring 'this satisfies the criteria.' Without human rule-making and standards bodies, accreditation does not exist.

A writ is a human-made formal written order or command issued by a court or other authoritative body. It exists only within legal and institutional frameworks, carrying the force of law. It is not a natural phenomenon but a construct of human governance, designed to compel action, grant permission, or record a judicial decision.

A subpoena is a human-made legal instrument — a formal written command issued by a court or authorized officer requiring a person to appear as a witness or produce documents. It exists solely within the constructed domain of law and governance. It compels participation in the justice process, an institution entirely human-made.

A bylaw is a rule or set of rules established by an organization, institution, or governing body to regulate internal conduct and operations. It is human-made — created deliberately through legislative or corporate processes — and built to persist through formal adoption, written codification, and institutional enforcement. Unlike natural customs, bylaws require explicit enactment and carry enforceable consequences.

A human-made representational system for organizing knowledge about domains — a structured map built through modeling, diagramming, and schema design to make complex information navigable and actionable.

Human-made body of traditional stories, customs, beliefs, and practices transmitted across generations within a community. Folklore is the map — the cultural framework through which groups encode shared knowledge, values, and identity — not the natural behaviors or oral traditions themselves.

A human-made construct: the concept and practice of declaring or performing an invocation to bring harm, misfortune, or divine judgment upon a target. Exists only as a cultural, religious, and linguistic construct — the map of a claimed causal power, never the natural world itself.

The human-made practice and theory of assigning meaning to signs, texts, behaviors, and phenomena — a culturally transmitted skill with parameters including interpreter, source, context, and interpretive framework. Persists through teaching, discipline, and discourse.

Human-made system of classification: the practice of creating structured categories to organize and distinguish phenomena by shared properties. The word itself is a construct — not any natural taxonomy but the human practice of building taxonomic frameworks.

The human-made linguistic practice of substituting milder, indirect, or inoffensive expressions for ones that may convey discomfort, offense, or bluntness. It persists through language use, teaching, and cultural transmission as a mechanism of face-management and social harmony.

The quorum is a human-made institutional rule establishing the minimum number of participants required for a collective decision to be valid. It is a constructed mechanism for ensuring legitimacy and preventing minority capture, existing solely as a social agreement about when deliberation counts.

A human-made court order that compels or prohibits specific action — an institutional mechanism for directing conduct through authorized command, persisting via written record and enforcement apparatus

Analogy is a human-made cognitive mechanism for understanding one concept (the target) in terms of another (the source), by mapping structural relationships between them. It is a tool of thought — a patterned transfer of inference across domains — invented, refined, and taught as a method of reasoning. It persists through language, education, and cultural transmission, and is a deliberate practice in science, pedagogy, and rhetoric.

Genre is a human-made classification system for creative works — literature, film, music, visual art — that groups productions by shared formal properties, conventions, and audience expectations. It is a map, not the works themselves.

Delegation is a human-made institutional mechanism that transfers authority or responsibility from one agent to another while preserving the delegator's ultimate accountability. It is not a natural phenomenon — every delegation requires a rule, a credential, or a social agreement that specifies what can be delegated, to whom, and under what conditions. The construct persists through documentation, credentialing systems, and the social practices of trust.

A human-made pedagogical technique: the deliberate construction of temporary support structures to enable a learner to accomplish tasks or develop understanding beyond their independent capability, with supports systematically reduced as competence grows. The construct itself — not any particular instructor or classroom — is what is catalogued here. Human-made because scaffolding is an explicitly designed instructional strategy, codified in educational theory (notably Vygotsky's zone of proximal development), and taught as a practice within teacher education and instructional design.

A topos is a recurring theme, motif, or argumentative pattern recognized across works of literature, rhetoric, and discourse — a shared conceptual resource humans built to structure meaning and signal familiar associations within a tradition.

The human-made construct of territorial or thematic authority boundaries — the institution that delineates who has the right to govern, judge, or regulate within a defined scope. Built to persist through legal codification and territorial mapping.

Testimony is the human-made institution of formally stated evidence given under prescribed rules — whether sworn in a court of law, deposed before a notary, or offered in a hearing. It does not exist in nature; it is a construct of law and procedure, created to transform speech or writing into recognized evidence. The map of testimony (the category, rules, and conventions by which communities decide what counts as testimony) is entirely human-made and persists through legal systems, institutional practice, and teaching.

A figure of speech employing deliberate understatement by negating the opposite — 'not bad' meaning 'good' — used across languages as a recognized rhetorical device for politeness, irony, and emphasis.

A human-made creative technique that imitates a specific source work, style, or genre through deliberate exaggeration, distortion, or incongruity. Built to persist through performance, text, and reproduction — it exists only as an authored act with intentionality.

A grievance is a human-made institutional mechanism for lodging a formal complaint within a legal, administrative, or organizational framework. It converts personal harm into a structured claim that triggers procedural response. The concept exists across cultures and epochs — from Athenian graphé to modern labor grievance procedures — as a durable social technology for managing conflict without violence.

Irony is a human-made figure of speech and cultural category for expressing meaning through the contrast between literal expression and intended sense. It persists through literary tradition, rhetorical education, and social practice — a tool of indirect communication built by language users across generations.

A trope is a human-made rhetorical and literary device — a conventional or figurative use of language that conveys meaning through recognizable, culturally shared patterns (metaphorical substitution, ironic inversion, repetitive structure). It is produced by speakers and writers drawing on linguistic conventions, persists through cultural transmission and literary education, and is unambiguously on the made side.
a formal legal procedure in which charges are read aloud to a defendant in open court and a plea is entered

The formal practice of recording disagreement with a collective decision — a human-made institutional mechanism that preserves minority views within deliberative bodies, persisting through written records, procedural rules, and the convention that minority positions deserve to be formally documented alongside majority outcomes.

appeal is a human-made institution — the formal mechanism for requesting review of a decision by a higher authority within an organized system. It persists through written rules, legal codes, institutional practice, and the language of hierarchy and error-correction.

A human-made knowledge organization technique: the practice of creating visual diagrams that map relationships between concepts using nodes, links, and linking phrases. Built as a tool for learning, design thinking, and knowledge elicitation — developed by Joseph Novak and colleagues at Cornell in the 1970s from Ausubel's meaningful learning theory. It persists through educational practice, cognitive science, and design methodologies.

Persuasion is a human-made institutional and communicative practice — the deliberate design of arguments, narratives, and rhetorical structures to shift another's beliefs, attitudes, or actions. It is not the natural inclination to agree; it is the engineered practice of persuasion, built to persist through rhetoric, propaganda, advertising, diplomacy, and law.

Arbitration is a human-made institution for resolving disputes outside formal courts. It is a structured procedure in which parties submit their conflict to one or more neutral third parties who render a binding or advisory decision. The map persists through language, formal rules, training, and the social practice of consent to arbitrate — it exists because humans built it to offload conflict resolution from public judiciary to private ordering.

A compact is a human-made institutional device — a formal agreement between parties that establishes mutual obligations and creates binding expectations. It persists through signature, recording, and the social practice of honoring commitments. Unlike a one-sided promise, a compact requires reciprocal acceptance and creates a shared framework of duties. The mechanism of persistence is collective recognition: a compact holds as long as the parties and their successors treat it as binding.
A human-made legal procedure: the act of recording testimony under oath before trial, governed by rules of evidence and procedure, built to preserve witness statements and allow discovery.

A worldview is a human-made conceptual framework — a structured set of assumptions, beliefs, and values through which individuals or cultures interpret reality and assign meaning. Made-side only (Law 1): it is not the world itself but the cognitive-institutional apparatus for mapping it. It persists through language, education, narrative, and cultural transmission — all human practices. Law 2a: the entry denotes the map of reality, never the actuality.
human-made social mechanism for reputation management, norm enforcement, and information sharing through informal verbal exchange within groups

The human-made institutional act of declaring one version, text, or instance as the authoritative reference for a class of things. It carves: selection of a single standard from multiple possible variants, backed by an authority's declaration, that serves as the reference against which non-canonical variants are measured, corrected, or excluded. It persists through institutional enforcement, citation, and reproduction.
a legal doctrine that bars a party from asserting a fact or right that contradicts a previous position they took or a representation they made, enforced by courts and sustained through precedent

A systematic pattern of deviation from rational judgment or normative inference in human decision-making. Cognitive biases are human-made constructs — categories developed by cognitive psychology and behavioral economics to describe predictable errors in thinking. The concept itself is a map of thinking patterns, not the raw cognitive faculty.

a human-made system of legal principles and remedies developed by the Court of Chancery to correct the rigidity and insufficiency of common law, persisting through precedent, judicial discretion, and the institutional memory of courts of conscience

Abduction is a human-constructed mode of reasoning — inference to the best explanation — invented by Charles Sanders Peirce to name the logical process by which we generate hypotheses from incomplete observations. It is a concept, not the act of guessing; the map of how humans form explanatory guesses, not the psychological process itself.

Satire is a human-made rhetorical and literary institution — a structured form of criticism that uses humor, irony, exaggeration, or ridicule to expose and challenge flaws in individuals, institutions, or cultural norms. It is a deliberate social mechanism for accountability through mockery, persisting through publication, performance, and cultural transmission across generations.

A human-made legal doctrine: the principle that courts should follow prior rulings when the same facts and legal questions arise again. It is the mechanism by which precedent binds future decisions, creating predictability and consistency in the law. The concept exists entirely on the made side — it is a rule of institutional practice, not a natural phenomenon.

A human-made software and organizational platform designed to facilitate citizen participation in governance, public deliberation, and collective action. It is an institution built from code, rules, and social contracts — persisting through digital infrastructure, community norms, and institutional memory.

A canon is a human-curated body of works, texts, or principles recognized as authoritative within a discipline, tradition, or institution. It is a map of cultural authority — what a community has collectively decided counts as exemplary or foundational — not the natural world.

The process and framework by which signs, symbols, and signals are generated, interpreted, and made meaningful — a human-made cognitive and social architecture for producing meaning through structured communication across individuals, disciplines, and media.

a human-made social information mechanism — the deliberate or accidental transmission of unverified claims across a social network, produced by and for collective sense-making; the natural fact of one person thinking another is unreliable does not qualify, but the construct 'rumour' as a category of social information is entirely human-made, emerging wherever humans gather and lack formal information channels

A presupposition is a human-made concept for the unstated assumptions that underlie and make possible any assertion, question, or communicative act. It is the map of what speakers and writers take for granted as background — a construct built by language users to track what must be accepted for discourse to function at all. The natural thing (pre-existing beliefs or expectations) is not the entry; the category 'presupposition' as used in linguistics, logic, and pragmatics is the map.

a human-made formal structure for deductive reasoning: two premises leading to a conclusion through a fixed pattern of terms. Created by Aristotelian logic to make valid inference patterns explicit, repeatable, and teachable

a human-made structured method of reasoning that stages opposing positions in dialogue to test, refine, and converge on truth or a higher understanding — persists through teaching, textual tradition, and practiced argument

Retroduction is a human-constructed mode of inference — reasoning from observed patterns or surprising consequents back to plausible explanatory hypotheses. It is a practice of the mind, part of the taxonomy of how humans justify beliefs, not a natural cognitive reflex. Built to persist through teaching, formal argument, and scientific method.

The human-made practice of structuring perception and interpretation by selecting and making salient certain aspects of reality while rendering others invisible. It persists through language, media, rhetoric, institutional design, and cultural teaching — the shared practice of framing how things are understood.

A fallacy is a pattern of reasoning that appears valid on the surface but is systematically unsound — a structured error that masquerades as sound inference. Human-made through centuries of logic, rhetoric, and cognitive science, it is a named category of faulty reasoning that persists through teaching, textbooks, and critical-instruction practices across disciplines.

The enthymeme is the human-made rhetorical device of a truncated syllogism — an argument deliberately structured with one premise left unstated, relying on the audience to supply it. It is a construct of persuasion, born in Aristotle's Rhetoric and sustained through centuries of debate, writing, and everyday argumentation.

A human-made method of reasoning from specific observations to general conclusions. It is a constructed inferential framework developed in philosophy and science, persisting through language, teaching, and formal logic.

Praxis is the human-made conceptual distinction between mere habit or technical skill and practice that is consciously informed by reflection and theory. It carves the institutionalized idea that action and thought should iteratively inform each other — persisting through educational systems, philosophical discourse, and professional training traditions.

The human-made epistemological position that no knowledge claim can be known with absolute certainty; all beliefs are provisional and subject to revision. It is a philosophical concept developed in the Western and Eastern traditions of inquiry, not a natural phenomenon.

the system of rules — phonological, morphological, syntactic, semantic — that a community invents to make its language work; it is not the language itself but the structured conventions that govern it, created and maintained through teaching and practice

A conjecture is a human-made epistemic tool: a proposition tentatively held as probably true without conclusive evidence. It is the bridge between observation and hypothesis, born of human reasoning and persisting through language, mathematical practice, and scientific method.

The human-made concept of cause and effect — a framework for linking events into explanatory chains. Humans invented causation to make sense of regularities in experience, to predict outcomes, and to assign responsibility. It persists through language, science, law, and everyday reasoning.

a criterion of scientific knowledge — the map of which claims admit of conceivable observation that could show them false. Human-made as the demarcation rule drawn by philosophers of science to separate testable theories from non-testable ones

deduction is a human-constructed mode of reasoning in which conclusions are guaranteed to follow necessarily from premises. It is a formal method for certifying that if the inputs hold, the outputs must — built by humans to transform uncertainty into logical certainty within argumentation.

Heuristics are human-constructed strategies and rules-of-thumb for reasoning, decision-making, and problem-solving under uncertainty. They are deliberately imperfect shortcuts — born of cognitive science, mathematics, and practical craft — that persist through education, documentation, and deployment in systems ranging from expert systems to everyday judgment. They are maps for navigating incomplete information, not the territory of any particular mind.

A lens is a human-made conceptual framework — a category, model, or interpretive scheme through which phenomena are structured and perceived. It is the map, not the territory: lenses such as the Marxist lens, feminist lens, or systems lens are analytical constructs developed in academic, political, and intellectual traditions. They do not exist in nature; they are tools of cognition invented by humans to organize experience, generate insight, and structure inquiry. Purely on the made side.

A human-made cognitive instrument for rendering phenomena intelligible — constructing causal, functional, or narrative accounts that link observed facts to underlying reasons, mechanisms, or purposes. The concept persists through language, education, and the disciplined practices of science, history, and everyday reasoning.
a human-made standard or rule established for judgment, evaluation, or decision — the map by which we decide whether something qualifies, passes, or belongs

The concept of generalization — not the biological tendency to generalize, but the human-constructed framework for reasoning from specific instances to broader rules. Built to persist through teaching, scientific method, and the formalization of inductive logic.

A notion is a human-made concept or idea — a mental category built to organize thought, communicate about the world, and reason about abstractions. It is the map of a cognitive unit, not the raw mental state itself. Human minds produce notions as tools for thinking, teaching, and shared understanding — they persist through language, writing, and cultural transmission.

A pattern is a human-made cognitive map — the recognized regularity, structure, or arrangement that humans abstract from data, phenomena, or behavior. It is the category and the recognition, not the raw occurrence itself.

A human-made cognitive concept: the capacity to represent and reason about one's own cognitive processes. Not the raw thinking faculty (natural), but the map — the category, framework, and practices humans built to reflect on, monitor, and regulate their own knowing.

Knowledge-representation is a human-made cognitive construct: the concept of encoding, structuring, and storing knowledge in accessible, manipulable forms. It is not the natural act of remembering (that is territory), but the map — the categories, formats, and media (language, writing, diagrams, databases, schemas) that humans built to externalize and share memory. It persists through teaching, writing systems, and formal notation, and it is entirely output by human making.

The human-made cognitive construct of a generalized idea or category that enables thought, communication, and reasoning. Concepts are mental tools humans create to group, classify, and manipulate experiences — they persist through language, teaching, and formal disciplines like logic and science.

The human-made concept of humor — the shared category and framework by which humans classify certain patterns, incongruities, and expressions as worthy of amusement. The laughter response is natural; the MAP of humor (cultural standards of what is funny, genres of comedy, the theory of incongruity, superiority, relief) is entirely human-made and persists through language, teaching, and cultural transmission.

A human-made computational paradigm that encodes information in quantum-mechanical states (superposition, entanglement) to perform operations impossible for classical machines. Built to persist as a mathematical framework, engineering discipline, and technological platform.
a human-made representation — a simplified construct designed to stand in for something else in thought, prediction, or explanation

The human practice of creating simplified models by deliberately ignoring irrelevant details — a method of abstraction used across science, mathematics, and engineering. It is made: designed, taught, and refined through centuries of scholarly practice. It persists through educational curricula, scientific methodology, and formal notation systems that transmit idealizing techniques across generations.

A human-made cognitive construct for grouping entities by shared properties. Categories are the basic units of conceptual organization, built through language, teaching, and cognitive practice. They persist as shared mental structures encoded in language and institutionalized through classification systems.

human-made: the act and artifact of making one thing stand for another. The natural world contains no stand-ins — representation is a cognitive and cultural practice whereby humans create substitutes (words, images, models, diagrams, code) that carry meaning about something else. Built to persist through teaching, documentation, and institutional memory.

A methodological principle of science: the requirement that a hypothesis or theory be structured so that empirical observation could demonstrate its falsehood. Human-made as a standard of scientific demarcation, introduced by Karl Popper to distinguish scientific from pseudoscientific claims. Built to persist through peer review, experimental design norms, and the reproducibility practices of scientific communities.

Formalism is a human-made epistemic practice: the construction of systems governed by explicit formal rules, symbols, and syntactic operations — independent of their empirical referents. It persists through teaching, institutionalization in mathematics and logic, and the formal languages of computing. It is the map of rule-bound reasoning, not any natural cognitive process.

The human practice of forming abstract ideas and mental categories from experience, observation, or other concepts — a cognitive tool for organizing thought that is made by the mind and persists through language, teaching, and discourse across generations.

A theoretical framework created by cognitive linguists Fauconnier and Turner to describe how humans integrate elements from distinct mental domains to generate new meaning, structure, and inference. It is a human-made map for a class of creative cognitive operations, persisting through academic discourse, pedagogical practice, and analytical application across disciplines.

The concept of epistemic violence — harm inflicted on a person's capacity as a knower through silencing, misrepresentation, or exclusion from knowledge production. It is a human-constructed framework originating in feminist and postcolonial critical theory (Spivak, Foucault) for diagnosing how power operates through the production and control of knowledge. The map persists through academic discourse, legal advocacy, and activist practice.

The standpoint from which a person or discipline views a subject — not the act of seeing itself (which is natural), but the constructed position shaped by language, culture, and experience. Human-made because it is a conceptual practice of orienting thought, not a biological faculty.

The human-made cognitive capacity to detect regularities, structures, and repetitions in sensory data, behavior, and experience. Built to persist through neural architecture, taught through examples, and formalized in algorithms and scientific methodology.

the human-made discipline and analytical framework for studying signs, symbols, and their role in producing meaning — how representation, communication, and interpretation are systematically understood across languages, texts, images, and media

Human-made concept for structural correspondence between distinct systems. The map of form-preservation across domains — not the natural structures themselves, but the human practice of recognizing and exploiting parallel organization in mathematics, psychology, linguistics, and design.

Decision-making is a human-constructed cognitive process for selecting among alternatives. It is an institution of deliberation, risk-assessment, and choice—built through language, models, and formal procedures like cost-benefit analysis, voting, and algorithmic selection. It persists through taught methods (decision trees, multi-criteria analysis), recorded protocols (standard operating procedures, corporate governance), and computational systems that encode choice frameworks.

A human-constructed organizing framework — a systematic plan or arrangement that structures elements, actions, or ideas into a coherent pattern for a purpose. It is the map of organized intention, not the organization itself.

The practice of constructing meaning from experience, especially under ambiguity. Developed as a formal concept by Kelly, Weick, and others, it names the human-made map of how agents interpret novel situations through iterative cycles of hypothesis, testing, and story. It is a cognitive technology for reducing uncertainty.

Modeling is the human-made practice of constructing simplified representations of systems, processes, or phenomena to understand, predict, or communicate about them. It is a cognitive tool that externalizes complex reality into tractable forms — diagrams, equations, physical mockups, computational simulations — built to persist across time through notation systems, documentation, and shared conventions.

A human-made artifact: a structured list of discrete items or steps recorded on a persistent medium for the purpose of verification, tracking completion, or ensuring no element is omitted in a process.

The human-made practice of combining distinct elements — ideas, objects, processes — into a coherent, integrated whole. Synthesis is not mere aggregation; it requires generative recombination that produces emergent structure. It persists through written compositions, oral traditions, creative and scientific practices, and the pedagogical transmission of methods.

Discourse is the human practice of structured communication within communities, institutions, and disciplines. It is not natural speech but a conventionally organized way of talking, writing, and arguing that follows rules of relevance, tone, and form specific to each context — from courtroom discourse to scientific discourse to everyday conversational discourse.

A human-made system of visual symbols, imagery, and conventional meanings used to communicate ideas within a culture, discipline, or medium. Built to persist through art, media, branding, and religious practice.

The human-made conceptual framework for assigning cause, responsibility, credit, or authorship to agents, actions, or outcomes. Humans invented attribution as a map to organize causality and accountability across social, legal, artistic, and scientific domains.

Semantics is the human-made construct of meaning — the system of conventions, rules, and practices by which humans assign, negotiate, and communicate significance in signs, symbols, language, and artifacts. It is the map of how meaning arises from the interaction between symbol and interpreter, not the natural world itself. Built to persist through language, teaching, and disciplinary practice.

A systematic record-keeping system for transactions, accounts, and balances. Human-made since ancient Sumeria — clay tablets tracking grain and livestock — and persisted through Roman tabularia, medieval merchant books, and modern blockchain ledgers. It is the institutionalized form of 'remembering who owes what,' engineered to persist across time and transfer trust between strangers.

Dogma is a human-made construct: a principle or set of principles laid down by an authoritative body (religious, political, scientific, or institutional) as incontrovertibly true, requiring unquestioning acceptance by adherents. It is human-made because it requires an authority to declare it, a community to adopt it, and mechanisms for transmission and enforcement. Without human authority and social transmission, dogma cannot exist.

Orthodoxy is the human-made practice of enforcing conformity to accepted doctrine or belief. It is a social technology for policing the boundaries of acceptable thought within a community, institution, or tradition — produced through mechanisms of approval, censure, and social sanction. It persists through institutional authority, social pressure, and the internalization of conformity norms.

A template is a human-made pattern, model, or framework designed to structure repeated actions, decisions, or artifacts. It is output by human design — not found in nature — and persists through language, teaching, and written reproduction. Templates exist across every domain: recipes in cooking, forms in administration, schemas in computing, plots in literature, procedures in engineering.

The human-made practice of creating a systematic list of items — goods, assets, materials, or data records — for the purposes of accounting, control, and verification. Inventory transforms the existence of things into a structured document that can be counted, audited, and managed; it is the map of what a collection contains at a given moment.

A human-made collection of texts or artifacts assembled, curated, and maintained as a structured body for analysis, reference, or study. It is an institution of curation — not a pile but a selected set organized by criteria its creators chose.
A human-made system for listing and organizing entries, objects, or records in a structured manner. Created to enable retrieval, navigation, and discovery of information through ordered enumeration.
A human-made representational symbol that bears resemblance to its referent, designed to persist through visual media, UI systems, and semiotic conventions for recognition and communication

A compilation is the human-made practice of gathering diverse items into a single organized collection for reference — anthologies, databases, compilations of data. It persists through editorial curation and the social act of presenting collected materials as a coherent whole.

A warranty is a human-made guarantee — a binding promise that a product, service, or claim will meet specified standards, backed by enforceable recourse if it does not. It persists through written contracts, legal enforcement, and institutional memory.

A codex is a human-made bound-book format and, by extension, a collected body of laws, rules, or knowledge organized under a single authority. It replaced the scroll as the dominant medium for structured written records in the ancient world and persists today as a metaphor for any compiled code of regulations or standards.

A stipulation is a human-made condition or requirement specified as part of a contract, legal proceeding, or formal agreement. It exists in the space of human making — the practice of defining precise terms within which parties operate. It persists through written instruments, recorded proceedings, and the legal/commercial systems that enforce them.

A benchmark is a human-made standard or reference point established for measurement, comparison, and evaluation. It is not a natural phenomenon but a conventional artifact built by institutions, professions, and markets to create common baselines for assessment. The word 'benchmark' names a constructed map — a calibrated reference — not any particular measured object.

A provision is a human-made clause or condition within a legal, contractual, or organizational text. It is a deliberate construct created to specify, reserve, or regulate a particular aspect of a larger agreement or framework. It persists through the text that contains it and the practices that enforce it.

A proxy is a human-made representational role: a person, entity, or system authorized to act on behalf of another within a legal, technical, or social framework. It is an institution of delegation — entirely constructed by human agreement, protocol, or law.

The signifier is a human-made semiotic construct: the perceptible form of a sign (sound-image, written mark, gesture) distinct from the concept it signifies. It is the map-side of the sign relation — the crafted vessel that carries meaning through language, writing, and cultural systems. Natural sounds and marks become signifiers only through human convention and semiotic practice.

A compendium is a human-made curated collection of information, systematically organized and recorded for reference. It is an institution of knowledge organization built to persist across time through documentation and cataloging practices.
A human-made curated collection of literary or artistic works assembled under a unifying theme or editor. Built to persist as a selection artifact that shapes how later readers encounter a tradition.

Syntax is a human-made system of rules governing the arrangement of elements in language, code, music, and other formal sign systems. It is not the natural impulse to communicate, but the constructed rules that make communication transmissible across time and distance.
Human-made practice of selecting, organizing, and preserving items of interest within a defined domain. Built to persist through systematic collection, cataloging, and stewardship.

A register is a human-made formal system of systematic record-keeping — an official catalog maintained by institutions to list, classify, and track entities (people, properties, vessels, species) with defined attributes. It is a bureaucratic artifact: the institutional practice of maintaining authoritative lists for governance, taxation, regulation, and accountability.

A citation is a human-made convention for referencing a source — a name, number, or marker that points to a specific document, work, or authority. It is institutional practice, not the source itself. Built to persist through citation styles (APA, MLA, Chicago, Bluebook) and the scholarly, legal, and editorial systems that enforce them.

A thesaurus is a human-made reference work that organizes words and their meanings into systematic groupings of synonyms, antonyms, and related terms. Built to persist through publication, digital indexing, and ongoing editorial revision.

A footnote is a human-made annotation placed outside the main text body — at the bottom of a page or at the end of a document — providing supplementary information, commentary, or citation without interrupting the primary narrative flow. It is an institution of textual scholarship, built to persist across editions and citations.

A seal is a human-made authentication mark — an embossed impression, stamped sigil, or wax impression applied to a document, object, or boundary to certify authenticity, authority, or confidentiality. It is institutional: its meaning comes from social recognition of the mark as a sign of verified origin, not from any natural property of the impression itself.
